name: Why is silicone caulk used instead of grout where the backsplash meets the countertop?

mainEntity.name: Why is silicone caulk used instead of grout where the backsplash meets the countertop?

acceptedAnswer.text: Colorado homes in the Denver and Centennial areas often experience structural shifting from expansive soils alongside dry indoor winter air. This seasonal movement causes expansion and contraction where the horizontal countertop meets the vertical drywall. Using hard grout in that interior corner almost always results in cracking over time. To prevent this, the bottom joint must be filled with a flexible, color-matched 100% silicone caulk rather than rigid grout. Silicone flexes during subtle framing shifts, maintaining a waterproof barrier behind your counters.
acceptedAnswer.description: Silicone caulk flexes during seasonal house shifting common in the Denver area, preventing the joint from cracking while maintaining a waterproof seal.
